claim_boundary: This contract fixes the states and mandatory evidence of an empirical documentation loop (capture statements and readers/sources, check the real effect, evidence differences, correct descriptive documentation, read back independently). It is a schema-level artifact checked against synthetic fixtures. It starts no workflow, owns no scheduler, task or worker, and does not claim that any host, instance or version currently runs the loop. Missing evidence means unknown, never success.

observed_from: BACH workflows help-forensic, help-expert-review, root-docs-review and docs-analyse (read-only)
BACH docs-maintenance dispatch and recurring state (read-only)

states.name: trigger_planned
states.meaning: A trigger is due or planned. This is a plan, not an execution.

states.name: task_created
states.meaning: A bounded analysis task exists and was read back from the task source.

states.name: executed
states.meaning: A real run happened and ended. The end state may be failed or unknown.

states.name: corrected
states.meaning: Descriptive documentation was changed to match the measured reality. Active readers and links were checked before any archival, and open wished-for requirements were kept as a target with a task.

states.name: reviewed
states.meaning: An independent read-back judged every difference exactly once.

states.name: repaired
states.meaning: A re-measurement with a verifiable record shows documentation and reality agree.

rules.monotonic: A chain contains each state at most once, in the order of this list, with non-decreasing observed_at. A later state never replaces the evidence of an earlier state.
rules.no_skipping: A state may only appear if all earlier states appear. The chain field unknown lists exactly the states without evidence.
rules.marker_is_not_evidence: A last-run or dispatch marker is only a trigger/dedup marker. It is never evidence for executed or any later state.
rules.task_status_is_not_evidence: A task status such as done is never evidence of execution or correction. Execution needs run_id, finished_at and result_id.
rules.failed_execution_stops: exit_state failed or unknown ends the chain at executed. Only succeeded with exit_code 0 may be followed by corrected.
rules.independent_review: reviewer_id and reviewer_instance must both differ from author_id and author_instance.
rules.hash_bound_correction: Every corrected file carries before_sha256 and after_sha256 (64 hex characters) and the two differ.
rules.verdict_coverage: reviewed carries exactly one verdict per difference, with unique valid difference_index values covering all differences.
rules.repair_needs_review: repaired needs reviewed, a verifiable remeasure record (reference, SHA-256, scope, ordered timestamp), remeasure.equal true and regression false.
rules.readback_is_evidence: task_created needs readback_verified true plus a readback reference and SHA-256.
rules.event_time_order: All event timestamps are timezone-aware ISO-8601, no later than their entry observed_at, and ordered along the chain: task creation, run start, run end, correction, review acceptance, measurement, repair.
rules.archival_needs_reader_check: An archive action is only valid with an archived_at timestamp in UTC and at least one reader check and one link check, none still active. Every checked_at lies at or after the observed_at of the executed entry, at or before archived_at, and at or before the observed_at of the corrected entry. Items with active readers are kept.
rules.open_requirements_kept: Every open wished-for requirement is kept as a target with a task_id; it is never dropped by a correction.
rules.interval_is_configuration: trigger_planned names the interval only as a reference to consumer configuration (form: config:, routine: or policy: followed by an identifier), never as a number of days or a duration. A purely numeric value or a time expression is not a reference.
rules.strict_types: Every mandatory collection and object has its exact type (list or object). A value of another type is an error of its own and is never treated as an empty list or skipped.

configuration_fields.note: Values are configuration of the consumer, never part of this contract.

next_gates: Adapter in the consuming system that fills the states from receipts (P3, owned by that system)
